newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to issue bonds to repay frozen savings.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to issue bonds to repay frozen savings.

text.p: Yugoslavia's government is set to issue state bonds to repay more than four billion dollars in frozen hard currency savings to its citizens before the end of the year, a senior government official said on Thursday.
"The state will declare those savings a public debt and issue bonds to service it," Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic told Reuters.
"The bonds will be denominated in German marks, targeted at Yugoslav citizens, but not for trade on the international markets," he added.
Yugoslav citizens have accumulated some 6.8 billion German marks in savings at the country's banks which were frozen by the cash-strapped government in 1991.

"We are now improving and fine-tuning our proposal to take into account our financial capacities. We want to resolve the problem in a realistic way. But the important thing is that the state is behind the project," the minister said.
Djunic said he could not yet give more details on the exact size and terms of the bond issue.
"Depositors will be offered to choose either to wait to be repaid in cash after a certain number of years or accept state bonds and use them in the privatisation process at face value," he said.

Djunic said the government preferred the latter solution since it would give a much-needed boost to the country's privatisation scheme and its dormant financial market. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
